notes:
This is the opening sheet of an English typescript letter addressed “Dear Kostant,” with a handwritten place read tentatively as Massy and the clear date 22. 10. 1969. The place/date stands at the upper right. The two quoted paper titles occur in the body, rather than as a heading. There is no signature, authorial page number or total-page count on this sheet; archive 21 is recorded only in a comment. The last question stops at “(they” and continues on the following supplied scan.

The writer says that Brieskorn's work on Klein singularities prompted a rereading of Kostant's papers, asks for later reprints, and proposes reconsideration in algebraic geometry. He then states counts for conjugacy classes of quadruples (T,B,T′,B′), where the maximal tori are “in apposition” and the Borels contain them. The first count is written with an ungrouped solidus, card(W)^2/hzφ(h); a second count, with a generating element specified, is card(W)^2/hz. The note at the foot states an extension for N(T)∩N(T′) and its order hzφ(h). These are assertions of the letter, not results established merely by transcribing it.

The questions and qualifications remain explicit: “I wonder if you know the answer to some of them”; “for some, or for all” quadruples whether the Borels are “in general position”; “Is there in any sense a distinguished conjugacy class”; and “What are the groups of automorphisms”. No general answer to the distinguished-class or automorphism questions was obtained here. The author’s literal “suggests number”, typed “polynomail” beneath a transposition curve, and “stablity” are retained. C_questions contrasts “suggests number” with “suggests a number”; this is not an actual C/H difference. Both supplied witnesses and the ink omit the article. The overlapping cells in appeared and automorphisms do not establish a correction chronology. The two insertion curves and the staggered footer annotation/order are drawn. Local uncertainty remains in the footer’s extension, hence and order; it is not silently removed by their grammatical plausibility.

Formula details prompted local ink checks: both raised 2 glyphs, the overwritten W, the two closed body phi forms, the two separately underlined typed Z letters, and the handwritten footer Z forms. The first exponent is definitely 2, but its faint impression does not securely identify the medium; H explicitly calls both 2s handwritten. The raised word generating has typewriter serifs, contrary to H’s editorial description. The final denominator Z in the footer retains a plain/double-struck doubt, while the other three integer Z forms have distinct doubled diagonals. The footer’s final standalone center Z is plain, and its open looped varphi differs graphically from the body’s crossed oval phi. These are ink decisions, not mathematical normalizations. The star remains outside the written cardinal expression; no denominator parentheses are added.

Actual checks were made separately and are documented in math_checks/123_022_counting_and_flags.md and the exact certificate. Conditional on one orbit of torus pairs, |W| Borels through each torus, N(T)∩B=T, T∩T′=e, and the stated common-normalizer order, a free action on |W|² Borel pairs gives |W|²/(hzφ(h)). Adding a choice among φ(h) generators gives |W|²/(hz), provided the common normalizer acts on that distinguished cyclic subgroup. This verifies the conditional counting implication. It does not prove those classification inputs or the general extension assertion. The type-A identity that an upper triangular monomial matrix is diagonal was rechecked directly. The readers also performed only the limited symbolic product/cancellation checks identified in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

For a concrete PGL₂ coordinate/Fourier pair, the common normalizer was computed as four projective classes I,X,Z,XZ, and all four choices of the two Borel flags are opposite; this gives one free orbit and agrees with h=2, z=2, φ(h)=1. Exact linear algebra over Q(i) also checked two PGL₄ coordinate/Fourier flag pairs: standard orders give opposite flags and a three-dimensional Borel Lie-algebra intersection, whereas using order (0,2,1,3) on both sides gives a common line in the two-dimensional flag steps and a four-dimensional intersection, which cannot be a maximal torus. The Fourier pair has a regular diagonal element acting by a Coxeter four-cycle and trivial torus intersection projectively. Identifying it with the precise cited terminology “in apposition” remains a background input, not an externally researched fact. Thus the negative answer to “for all” is conditional on that identification. The letter asks the question; no asserted conclusion in its text is replaced or corrected by this example.
